# Purpose

<!-- State the report question, intended reader, downstream use, and source-data version. -->


<!-- Adapt this document for the species during `index-compile-data`. It reads bottom-trawl
data from the IMR Biotic database and, optionally, legacy SPD files; applies the
quantitative-catch filtering from index-wise's `data-filtering.md`; removes duplicates;
computes swept-area density; and saves a compiled dataset with true zeros to the root-level
data/output. This document is the survey-selection document: keep survey positions, gear,
timing, catch/occurrence, and filtering decisions here. The companion
{{SPECIES_SLUG}}-{{REGION_SLUG}}-data-report.qmd is the compiled-data overview.
Needs access to the IMR Biotic database and an IMR intranet connection. Do NOT hard-wrap prose. -->

This document and the associated analyses are based on [index-wise](https://github.com/DeepWaterIMR/index-wise) and were developed with researcher-supervised generative AI. Station catch data are acquired from the **IMR Biotic database** when this [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) document is compiled.

A survey means one cruise. A survey is included when at least one positive target-species catch passes the standard haul filters and lies inside the prediction region. Included surveys with a cruise-series code are assigned to that cruise series, where a cruise series means all surveys belonging to one time-series. For each included survey, retain all valid regional hauls assigned to that survey so stations without the target species remain true zeros. Other surveys in the same cruise series may be dropped when they do not contain a qualifying target catch or do not meet the sampling-quality criteria. Assess surveys without a cruise-series code individually and group them under `Other` only after they qualify.

## Scope

This document selects surveys from the IMR Biotic database for the configured prediction region. The polygon map below shows all configured region features; the active region is selected by `config.yaml`.

When survey acquisition uses a broader reporting polygon than the later model domain, set `ACQUISITION_REGION` and `ACQUISITION_REGION_LAYER` in `config.yaml`, keep `REGION` as the model domain, and set `ADD_REGION_IDENTIFIER: true` with `PARTITION_REGION` and `PARTITION_REGION_LAYER`. The compiler should qualify surveys and retain hauls across the full acquisition polygon, then add a `region` column identifying the model-domain partition (for example `S62`) versus the remainder of the acquisition polygon (for example `NS`).

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#| label: fig-prediction-region
#| fig-cap: "Prediction polygons over quality-filtered positive target-species hauls across the full study extent. The configured region is used for survey selection; other polygons are shown for context or later regional indices."
source(here::here("R", "0_setup.R"))
# Build `positive_observations` from the IMR Biotic database using the standard data-quality
# filters, without restricting the map query to the active prediction-region polygon. This keeps
# split-region overview maps from omitting observations in neighbouring regions.
prediction_regions <- sf::st_read(
  here::here(cfg$REGION_FILE),
  layer = cfg$REGION_LAYER,
  quiet = TRUE
) |>
  sf::st_transform(cfg$MAP_CRS %||% 3995)
map_crs <- sf::st_crs(prediction_regions)
region_bbox <- sf::st_bbox(prediction_regions) |>
  sf::st_as_sfc() |>
  sf::st_cast("POINT")
region_values <- setNames(
  grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("#3288bd", "#d53e4f"))(
    length(unique(prediction_regions$region))
  ),
  sort(unique(prediction_regions$region))
)
positive_bbox <- sf::st_as_sf(
  positive_observations,
  coords = c("longitudestart", "latitudestart"),
  crs = 4326,
  remove = FALSE
) |>
  sf::st_transform(map_crs) |>
  sf::st_bbox() |>
  sf::st_as_sfc() |>
  sf::st_cast("POINT")

ggOceanMaps::basemap(
  data = c(region_bbox, positive_bbox),
  shapefiles = cfg$MAP_SHAPEFILES %||% "Arctic",
  bathymetry = TRUE,
  bathy.style = "rbg",
  legends = FALSE,
  base_size = 8,
  expand.factor = 1.1
) +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(
    data = prediction_regions,
    ggplot2::aes(fill = .data$region),
    alpha = 0.25,
    colour = "grey20",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = region_values, name = "Prediction region") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude", fill = "Prediction region") +
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(
    data = positive_observations,
    ggplot2::aes(x = .data$longitudestart, y = .data$latitudestart),
    colour = "#b2182b",
    alpha = 0.55,
    size = 1.4
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::coord_sf(expand = FALSE)
```

## Surveys and cruise series

A survey means one cruise. A survey is included when at least one positive target-species catch passes the standard haul filters inside the prediction region. A cruise series groups surveys belonging to one time-series; surveys that do not qualify are not backfilled merely because they share a cruise-series code. The table below is a generic audit pattern: adapt the compiler's survey-audit object when it contains mission-level inclusion details.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-survey-selection
survey_table <- dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(cruiseseries) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `First year` = min(startyear, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Last year` = max(startyear, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Retained hauls` = dplyr::n(),
    `Positive hauls` = sum(biomass > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Positive catch (kg)` = round(sum(biomass, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    `Zero fraction (%)` = round(100 * mean(biomass == 0, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(`Cruise series` = cruiseseries)
knitr::kable(
  survey_table,
  caption = "Cruise-series audit for qualifying target-species surveys. Zero fraction is the percentage of retained bottom-trawl hauls without the target species."
)
```

## Filtering decisions — station filter {#sec-filtering-decisions}

Follow index-wise `data-filtering.md`. The `samplequality` rule is conditional on the cruise series, and the accepted `gearcondition` codes require survey-specific justification. Together with `stationtype`, these fields define the candidate quantitative hauls. The filtering expression is shown in @lst-filter-expression.

If a cruise series has a documented exception, explain it here. For example, CoastalS (code 23) accepts sample-quality values 1 and 2, whereas other cruise series require value 1. Code 2 identifies hauls targeted using acoustic registrations or other information about fish. CoastalS surveys in the early years targeted saithe acoustically; retaining code 2 therefore requires a documented argument that this selection mechanism remains compatible with the target-species estimand.

```{r}
#| lst-label: lst-filter-expression
#| lst-cap: "SQL-compatible haul filter applied before collection; the sample-quality rule is applied immediately after collection."
#| code-fold: false
#| eval: false
accepted_gearcondition <- c(1, 2) # verify against the survey protocol/reference codes

stnall |>
  dplyr::filter(
    gearcategory == "Bottom trawls",
    missiontypename %in% c("Forskningsfartøy", "Leiefartøy"),
    startyear >= cfg$FIRST_YEAR,
    startyear <= last_complete_year,
    !is.na(distance),
    !is.na(latitudestart),
    !is.na(longitudestart),
    latitudestart > 0,
    gearcondition %in% accepted_gearcondition,
    is.na(stationtype) | !stationtype %in% c("C", "2", "A", "E"),
    distance >= 0.3,
    distance <= 5,
    dplyr::if_else(
      !is.na(.data$cruiseseriescode) & .data$cruiseseriescode == "23",
      .data$samplequality %in% 1:2,
      .data$samplequality %in% 1
    )
  )
```

```{r station-filter, eval=params$recompile}
accepted_gearcondition <- c(1, 2) # verify against the survey protocol/reference codes

stn <- stnall |>
  dplyr::filter(
    gearcategory == "Bottom trawls",
    missiontypename %in% c("Forskningsfartøy", "Leiefartøy"),
    startyear >= cfg$FIRST_YEAR,
    startyear <= last_complete_year,
    !is.na(distance), !is.na(latitudestart), !is.na(longitudestart),
    latitudestart > 0,
    gearcondition %in% accepted_gearcondition,
    is.na(stationtype) | !stationtype %in% c("C", "2", "A", "E"),
    distance >= 0.3, distance <= 5
    # is.na(gear) | !gear %in% obsolete_gear_codes, # add non-missing survey-specific obsolete gear codes
    # cruiseseries %in% cfg$SURVEYS             # restrict to the chosen surveys
  ) |>
  dplyr::collect() |>
  dplyr::filter(
    dplyr::if_else(
      !is.na(.data$cruiseseriescode) & .data$cruiseseriescode == "23",
      .data$samplequality %in% 1:2,
      .data$samplequality %in% 1
    )
  )

if ("missionid" %in% names(stn)) {
  stn <- stn |>
    dplyr::mutate(haul_id = paste(missionid, serialnumber, sep = "_"))
} else {
  stn <- stn |>
    dplyr::mutate(haul_id = paste(missiontype, startyear, platform, missionnumber,
                                  serialnumber, sep = "_"))
}

# Russian data are INCLUDED by default. To exclude (config INCLUDE_RUSSIAN: false):
if (!isTRUE(cfg$INCLUDE_RUSSIAN))
  stn <- dplyr::filter(stn, !nation %in% c("140", "90"))
```

## Remove duplicates

A fishstation can contain several catchsamples or catch parts for one species. Their relationship must be resolved from identifiers, product and raising fields, and comments before additive parts are aggregated. The following diagnostic then flags haul/species combinations where the summed length sample exceeds the summed catch; it does not by itself identify overlapping catchparts.

```{r duplicates, eval=params$recompile}
dupe_ids <- stn |>
  dplyr::filter(commonname %in% filter_sp) |>
  dplyr::group_by(cruiseseriescode, haul_id, commonname) |>
  dplyr::reframe(
    catchweight        = sum(catchweight, na.rm = TRUE),
    catchcount         = sum(catchcount, na.rm = TRUE),
    lengthsampleweight = sum(lengthsampleweight, na.rm = TRUE),
    lengthsamplecount  = sum(lengthsamplecount, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(catchcount < lengthsamplecount | catchweight < lengthsampleweight)

dir.create(here::here("ai", "review"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
readr::write_csv(dupe_ids, here::here("ai", "review", "duplicate-station-report.csv"))
stn <- dplyr::filter(stn, !haul_id %in% dupe_ids$haul_id)
```

## True zeros and swept-area density

Keep stations with no catch of the target species as real zeros, then compute density. Gear width follows `config.yaml` `GEAR_WIDTH` (see the gear-width note there).

```{r response, eval=params$recompile}
gear_width_m <- function(geartype) {
  if (is.numeric(cfg$GEAR_WIDTH)) {
    rep(as.numeric(cfg$GEAR_WIDTH), length(geartype))
  } else if (identical(cfg$GEAR_WIDTH, "per_gear")) {
    dplyr::case_when(geartype == "Shrimp" ~ 25, geartype == "Cod" ~ 25 * 3.746,
                     TRUE ~ NA_real_)
  } else {
    as.numeric(cfg$GEAR_WIDTH)          # single set width; keep geartype in the model formula
  }
}

dt <- stn |>
  # join target-species catch onto the full retained-station set so absences become zeros:
  dplyr::mutate(
    biomass   = dplyr::coalesce(catchweight_sp, 0),   # <- adapt to your join of species catch
    count     = dplyr::coalesce(catchcount_sp, 0),
    gear_width = gear_width_m(geartype),
    swept_area = distance * (gear_width / 1852),        # nmi^2
    rho_biomass   = biomass / swept_area,
    rho_abundance = count   / swept_area
  )

# Fill missing/invalid bottom depth from GEBCO:
dt$depth <- ggOceanMaps::get_depth(
  dplyr::rename(dt, lon = longitudestart, lat = latitudestart),
  bathy.style = "rc", bind = FALSE
)

cruise_series_levels <- sort(unique(dt$cruiseseries))
cruise_series_cols <- setNames(
  grDevices::colorRampPalette(c(
    "#9e0142", "#d53e4f", "#f46d43", "#fdae61", "#fee08b",
    "#e6f598", "#abdda4", "#66c2a5", "#3288bd", "#5e4fa2"
  ))(length(cruise_series_levels)),
  cruise_series_levels
)
```

## Data overview

The compiled dataset was extracted from the IMR Biotic database on `r compile_metadata$data_downloaded_at_label`. It should contain retained bottom-trawl hauls from the configured year range, including both target-positive hauls and true-zero hauls. The retained-haul count is `nrow(dt)` after catchsample rows have been aggregated to haul identifiers; do not count a `serialnumber` and `startyear` combination as a haul by itself. The compact Results overview is shown in @tbl-data-overview.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data-overview
overview <- dt |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Retained hauls` = format(dplyr::n(), big.mark = " "),
    `Positive hauls` = format(sum(rho_biomass > 0, na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = " "),
    `True-zero hauls` = format(sum(rho_biomass == 0, na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = " "),
    `Included surveys (cruises)` = format(dplyr::n_distinct(cruise, startyear, platformname, na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = " "),
    `First year` = min(startyear, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Last year` = max(startyear, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Cruise series` = format(dplyr::n_distinct(cruiseseries), big.mark = " ")
  )
overview_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(
  overview,
  dplyr::everything(),
  names_to = "Metric",
  values_to = "Value"
) |>
  tibble::add_row(Metric = "Latest trawl haul", Value = latest_haul_label, .before = 1)
knitr::kable(
  overview_long,
  caption = "Compact overview of the extracted and filtered target-species data."
)
```

## Survey catch and effort

These figures separate total target catch from the number of positive hauls. True-zero hauls remain in the retained effort but do not contribute to positive catch totals.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#| label: fig-survey-catch-overview
#| fig-cap: "Total target-species catch and number of positive hauls by cruise series in the {{REGION_SLUG}} prediction region. The panels use independent y-axis scales."
cruise_series_levels <- sort(unique(dt$cruiseseries))
cruise_series_cols <- setNames(
  grDevices::colorRampPalette(c(
    "#9e0142", "#d53e4f", "#f46d43", "#fdae61", "#fee08b",
    "#e6f598", "#abdda4", "#66c2a5", "#3288bd", "#5e4fa2"
  ))(length(cruise_series_levels)),
  cruise_series_levels
)
survey_summary <- dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(cruiseseries) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    catch_t = sum(biomass, na.rm = TRUE) / 1000,
    positive_hauls = sum(biomass > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(catch_t, positive_hauls), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value")
ggplot2::ggplot(survey_summary, ggplot2::aes(cruiseseries, value, fill = cruiseseries)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~measure, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = cruise_series_cols) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(guide = ggplot2::guide_axis(angle = 90)) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Cruise series", y = NULL, fill = "Cruise series") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Gear overview

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#| label: fig-gear-overview
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Overview of bottom-trawl gear used in the included {{REGION_SLUG}} cruise series. Panel A shows catch by gear filled by cruise series; Panel B shows haul counts by year and broad gear type."
gear_axis <- function(values, offset = 0.01) {
  values <- values[is.finite(values)]
  max_value <- max(values, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_exponent <- if (max_value > 0) ceiling(log10(max_value)) else -2
  axis_values <- c(0, 10 ^ seq(-2, max_exponent, by = 1))
  axis_values <- axis_values[axis_values <= max_value | axis_values == 0]
  axis_labels <- format(axis_values, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE, digits = 15, big.mark = " ")
  axis_labels <- sub("0+$", "", axis_labels)
  axis_labels <- sub("[.]$", "", axis_labels)
  list(breaks = axis_values + offset, labels = axis_labels)
}
gear_axis <- gear_axis(dt$biomass)
p_gear <- ggplot2::ggplot(dt, ggplot2::aes(gearname, biomass + 0.01, fill = cruiseseries)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot() +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10(breaks = gear_axis$breaks, labels = gear_axis$labels) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = cruise_series_cols) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Gear", y = "Catch (kg)", fill = "Cruise series") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
p_year <- dt |>
  dplyr::count(startyear, geartype) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(startyear, n, fill = geartype)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col() +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2030, 5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(c(0, 0.05))) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Year", y = "Number of trawl hauls", fill = "Gear type") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()
cowplot::plot_grid(p_gear, p_year, labels = "AUTO", ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(6, 4))
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#| label: tbl-gear-overview
knitr::kable(
  dt |>
    dplyr::group_by(cruiseseries, geartype, gearname) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      hauls = dplyr::n(),
      mean_distance_nmi = mean(distance, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_duration_min = mean(duration_min, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ),
  caption = "Gear, effort, and haul characteristics by cruise series."
)
```

## Survey timing

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#| label: fig-survey-timing
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-cap: "Timing of individual surveys by cruise series. Segments span the first to last valid haul date within each cruise."
timing <- dt |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(station_date), !is.na(cruise)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(startyear, cruise, cruiseseries) |>
  dplyr::summarise(first_date = min(station_date), last_date = max(station_date), .groups = "drop")
ggplot2::ggplot(timing, ggplot2::aes(first_date, startyear, colour = cruiseseries)) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(ggplot2::aes(xend = last_date, yend = startyear), linewidth = 2) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = cruise_series_cols) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Date", y = "Survey year", colour = "Cruise series") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor.y = ggplot2::element_blank())
```
